topic: Earth's Tilt and Its Effect on Seasons
key_concepts: Earth's rotation on its axis causes day and night
Earth's revolution around the Sun takes about 365.25 days
Earth's axis is tilted 23.5 degrees relative to its orbit
The tilt of Earth's axis causes different parts of Earth to receive varying amounts of sun
Sunlight strikes the equator more directly or perpendicularly, producing warmer temperatur
At higher latitudes near the poles, sunlight strikes at a more oblique angle, spreading en
Latitude affects the intensity of solar radiation and heat received
Longer daylight hours mean more solar energy received
Earth's position in its orbit affects the Sun's altitude and path in the sky
The Sun's angle at noon affects the amount of energy received
Seasonal changes include differences in the length of daylight and night
At an equinox, the Sun is directly overhead at noon at the equator
